concept.name: Governance token
concept.definition: A governance token is a token whose primary utility is voting power over a protocol's decisions — parameter changes, treasury spending, upgrades — typically exercised through a DAO's proposal-and-vote contracts.
concept.intuition: It is a shareholder ballot in token form: holding it gives you a say in how the protocol runs, weighted by how much you hold.
concept.mechanics: Holders (or their delegates) create and vote on proposals; if quorum and majority thresholds pass, execution happens automatically or via timelocked multisig (e.g. UNI: 1% of supply to propose, 4% quorum, 7-day voting, 2-day timelock). Many governance tokens also carry fee-switch or value-accrual potential, but voting power itself is the core function.
concept.failure_modes: Low participation lets small coalitions or whales capture governance; vote-buying, bribery markets and flash-loan governance attacks can pass malicious proposals; delegation concentrates effective power in a few hands.
concept.misconceptions: A governance token is not equity — it usually grants no legal claim on revenue or assets, only on-chain voting rights. 'Decentralized governance' in practice often means a handful of delegates and a multisig execute most decisions.
concept.example: UNI holders can vote to activate Uniswap's protocol fee switch or spend the community treasury (43% of supply); ENS holders instead delegate their votes to community stewards who vote on their behalf.
